gilino-R8572.summary: "El Gilino", a Sforza agent at the imperial court, writes from Paredes de Nava on 15 September 1527 to Francesco II Sforza, Duke of Milan, at Cremona: Gattinara is out of favour over two intercepted letters to the Viceroy of Naples about relieving Genoa; the Duke should have the Bilia keep in with Gattinara now that Bourbon is dead; papal briefs, the Abbatino's mission, the French ambassadors insisting the Duke keep Milan, and the investiture of Milan sent to the Infante with 100,000 ducats.
gilino-R8572.en:
I am assured by many that [?His] Lordship stands in little favour with the Emperor for one single thing that is
imputed to him, and on account of two letters of his, intercepted, to the Viceroy, that he should send the galleys of
Naples to the relief of Genoa and order Lope de Soria to use the rest of the hundred thousand ducats of the exchange
for the benefit of that city, both in provision of cash and of victuals, since otherwise the whole would be lost.
[?His] detractors, who openly are the confessor and [?the German] secretary, will have it that Lautrec, on such
information, sent part of the troops [?…] to the siege of Genoa which were destined for another place, and that for
this the said city [?…] was no longer defended, [?for] the great need that I see His Majesty has of him.

system: Sforza chancery cipher: barred base signs (G written like 6, B, D, d, o, H, A, P, R) with two-digit numbers for syllables in ordered rows (B.31-50 ba..gu, B.51-54 fa..fo, D.51-65 la..nu, 6.56-80 pa..tu, o.33-47 va..zu), about forty unnumbered signs for…
